I used the two-point Arrhenius equation:
ln(k₂/k₁) = (Eₐ/R)(1/T₁ − 1/T₂)

- T₁ = 353.15 K and T₂ = 393.15 K, so 1/T₁ − 1/T₂ = 2.881×10⁻⁴ K⁻¹.
- Eₐ/R = 75,000 / 8.314 = 9,020 K.
- ln(k₂/k₁) = 2.599, so k₂/k₁ = 13.45.
- k₂ = 1.2×10³ × 13.45 = 1.61×10⁴ s⁻¹.

I checked the arithmetic with a short Python run, which gave a ratio of 13.447 and k₂ = 16,137 s⁻¹. This assumes the activation energy stays the same between 80 °C and 120 °C. I didn't create any files.
